title: Deriving proper/open support under all-sheaf finite cohomological dimension
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $p:V\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and set $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the uncompleted unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Assume $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and assume an integer $d\geq0$ satisfies $R^qp_*F=0$ for every pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $V$ and $q>d$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\gamma:i_!r_*\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*k_!$ for the specified sheaf comparison [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison], and use exact extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. For $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, choose a K-injective representative $J$ with injective terms [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and a K-injective resolution $k_!J\to I$. The map represented by
$$i_!r_*J\xrightarrow{\gamma_J}p_*k_!J\longrightarrow p_*I$$
defines an isomorphism $\Gamma_M:i_!Rr_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*k_!M$, independent of the choices and natural in $M$. With the canonical restriction isomorphism $\lambda$ of [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction], its specified normalization under $i_!\dashv i^*$ [prop-exc-open-adjoint] is
$$\lambda_M\circ i^*\Gamma_M=1_{Rr_*M},\qquad \Gamma_M=\varepsilon_i\circ i_!(\lambda_M^{-1}).$$
No quasi-compactness of $i$ or boundedness or etale-origin condition on $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the small skeleton and coefficient universe specified for each small pro-etale site. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], its category of constant-$A$ module sheaves is Grothendieck abelian and admits functorial K-injective replacements with injective terms. Represent $M$ by such a complex $J$. Exactness of $k_!$ in [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $k_!J$ represent $k_!M$; choose a replacement $a:k_!J\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and degreewise injective. The operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] compute $Rr_*M$ by $r_*J$ and $Rp_*k_!M$ by $p_*I$. Exactness of $i_!$ computes $i_!Rr_*M$ by $i_!r_*J$. Thus these are representatives in exactly the ordinary, uncompleted unbounded categories of the statement.

source.place: Tag 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); ringed-site application: sites-cohomology.tex, Section 07A5; injectives.tex, Theorem 079P

proof.text: For each $s\in\mathbf Z$, $J^s$ is an injective module sheaf on $U$. The Cartesian square, properness of $p$, finite constant coefficient ring, and the all-sheaf bound $d$ satisfy precisely the hypotheses of [lem-exc-proetale-cartesian-open-injective-acyclic]. It gives $R^qp_*(k_!J^s)=0$ for every $q>0$. Each $I^s$ is also $p_*$-acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing], since it is injective. These are termwise acyclicity statements, not a claim that $k_!$ preserves injectives. Neither argument requires a lower bound on $s$ or quasi-compactness of the open.

source.place: Retained repaired proof Step 3: injective-acyclicity input; etale analogue only, more-etale.tex Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), case (b)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex] to $F=p_*$ between the module-sheaf categories. The source is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; the target is abelian, and $p_*$ is additive and left exact by its sectionwise definition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] (kernels are computed sectionwise). Its finite-CD hypothesis is exactly the assumed vanishing for every module sheaf on $V$; in Tag 07K7 take $n=d+1$. Step 2 makes both $k_!J$ and $I$ eligible for that lemma. Its natural comparison gives
$$\alpha_I\circ Q(p_*a)=Rp_*(Qa)\circ\alpha_{k_!J}.$$
Both $\alpha$ components are isomorphisms and $Qa$ is an isomorphism, so $Q(p_*a)$ is an isomorphism. Apply the specified natural sheaf isomorphism [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison] degreewise to get a chain isomorphism $\gamma_J:i_!r_*J\to p_*k_!J$. Its composite with $p_*a$ therefore defines the required isomorphism $\Gamma_M$.

source.place: Tag 07K7 (lemma-unbounded-right-derived), (1)-(2) and naturality of the derived comparison

proof.text:
Here is the choice and morphism check for that composite. A morphism $M\to M'$ is represented by a chain map $h:J\to J'$ unique up to homotopy, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Write $a':k_!J'\to I'$ for the second replacement. Since $I'$ is K-injective and $Qa$ is invertible, the same Hom bijection produces $b:I\to I'$ with $ba$ homotopic to $a'k_!h$, uniquely up to homotopy. Applying additive $p_*$ preserves that homotopy. Naturality of $\gamma$ in [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison] then gives
$$Q(p_*b)\circ\Gamma_M=\Gamma_{M'}\circ Q(i_!r_*h).$$
These outer maps compute the derived images by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; hence this is naturality in $M$. Changing $h$, $b$, or $a$ changes no map in the localization. For different representatives or replacements, perform the same construction over $1_M$; the Hom bijection gives the canonical comparison isomorphisms and the same equation identifies the two displayed composites. Thus the resulting map is independent of every choice.

Compute its restriction using [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction]. This node supplies the normalization $i^*p_*I=r_*k^*I$ on [def-pur-kinjective-complex], asserts that $k^*I$ is K-injective, and identifies $k^*k_!J$ with $J$ by the open unit [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit]. Exact $k^*$ turns $a$ into a quasi-isomorphism; write $c:J\to k^*I$ for $k^*a$ composed with that unit. Thus $r_*c$ is the comparison between the two K-injective computations of $Rr_*M$. The sheaf normalization of [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison] says that $i^*\gamma_J$ is the identity after these open-unit and restriction identifications. Consequently $i^*\Gamma_M$ is represented by $r_*c:r_*J\to r_*k^*I$. By the specified normalization of the derived restriction node, $\lambda_M$ is represented by the inverse of this comparison. Therefore
$$\lambda_M\circ i^*\Gamma_M=1_{Rr_*M}.$$
This checks the specified morphism itself, rather than just comparing the two objects.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives); Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective); termwise open restriction as specified in the cited nodes

proof.text:
Let $X=Rr_*M$ and $Y=Rp_*k_!M$. Under the derived adjunction $i_!\dashv i^*$ of [prop-exc-open-adjoint], a map $t:i_!X\to Y$ corresponds to $i^*t\circ\eta_X:X\to i^*Y$. The open-unit identification in [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction] (using [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit]) identifies $\eta_X$ with the identity; thus Step 5 says that the adjunct of $\Gamma_M$ is $\lambda_M^{-1}$. The inverse adjunction formula sends $s:X\to i^*Y$ to $\varepsilon_Y\circ i_!s$. It gives exactly
$$\Gamma_M=\varepsilon_i\circ i_!(\lambda_M^{-1}).$$
All hypotheses used were the stated all-sheaf finite-CD bound and proper/open Cartesian geometry. No truncation, completion, constructibility, etale-origin condition, or quasi-compactness of $i$ has entered.
